outro_script: And that's all the circuits for today's robotics roundup! From RoboParty's new RP1 to open-source dreams, keep those gears turning. Have a fantastic rest of your day!

items.title: RoboParty Unveils RP1 Humanoid at IROS, Plans Broader Open-Source Release in Q4
items.summary: RoboParty unveiled the RP1 humanoid robot at IROS on September 28th. This robot demonstrates balance recovery capabilities and peak joint torques up to 160 N·m. Broader releases of the RP1, including the full stack, are planned for the fourth quarter. The company intends to progressively release motion control, simulation environments, SDKs, and PartyOS to the community. Developers can access resources from the earlier ROBOTO ORIGIN repository as a starting point.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, RoboParty Unveils RP1 Humanoid at IROS, Plans Broader Open-Source Release in Q4. This report details the unveiling of the RP1 humanoid robot at IROS and its demonstrated capabilities. At the event on September 28th, the RP1 humanoid robot was presented, showcasing advanced balance recovery capabilities and the ability to achieve peak joint torques up to 160 Newton-meters. The company has scheduled broader releases of the RP1, including the full stack, for the fourth quarter. Plans involve the progressive release of motion control, simulation environments, software development kits, and PartyOS to the community. Developers are directed to the earlier ROBOTO ORIGIN repository for initial resources. This progression indicates an increased focus on democratizing access to advanced humanoid robotics technology within the development community.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: RobotCAD v12.10.0 is released!
items.summary: RobotCAD v12.10.0 has been released, introducing several new features and fixes. New additions include a RobotCAD MCP server for agentic robot assembling and an updated Models Library with faster import capabilities for xacro and mjcf models. The release also added a sensors field of view feature and improved compatibility for external document links and coordinate systems. Furthermore, it includes support for Sverk, an aerial robot framework, and a vacuum gripper tool for Gazebo.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: RobotCAD v12.10.0 is released!". This report details the release of RobotCAD version twelve point ten point zero, introducing several new features and necessary fixes. The update includes a new RobotCAD MCP server designed for agentic robot assembling and an updated Models Library featuring faster import capabilities for xacro and mjcf models. Additionally, the release incorporated a sensors field of view feature and enhanced compatibility for external document links and coordinate systems. Support was also added for the Sverk aerial robot framework and a vacuum gripper tool for Gazebo. This update signals continued development in robotics simulation and software tooling. Further developments in agentic systems and simulation environments are anticipated.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Has anyone found a reliable way to validate a hand eye calibration result?
items.summary: Finding a reliable method to validate hand-eye calibration results remains an unresolved issue. Existing tools provide reprojection error or transform data, but there is no clear consensus on how to trust these results. Visual inspection in RViz is insufficient for proper validation, especially concerning scale. The author seeks practical methods, such as validation motions or comparing against measured poses, that do not require expert judgment. Ultimately, the community needs to establish a standard procedure for confirming the accuracy of these calibration results.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Has anyone found a reliable way to validate a hand eye calibration result?". This report addresses the ongoing challenge of establishing a reliable method for validating hand-eye calibration results within the robotics community. Existing tools provide reprojection error or transform data, but a consensus on trusting these results remains absent. Visual inspection within visualization environments like RViz is noted as insufficient for proper validation, particularly concerning scale. The author seeks practical methods, such as validation motions or comparison against measured poses, that bypass the need for expert judgment. The community requires the establishment of a standardized procedure for confirming the accuracy of these calibration results. This pursuit is essential for advancing the trustworthiness of spatial data in robotics applications.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Tuning StereoSGBM on PS5 Camera (ROS 2 Galactic) for Dense Depth Maps
items.summary: A user is attempting to tune StereoSGBM parameters in ROS 2 Galactic for dense depth map estimation from a PS5 stereo camera. The goal is to produce a dense point cloud suitable for 3D reconstruction using RTAB-Map. The user is struggling to achieve smooth depth maps, as adjustments lead to outputs that are either extremely sparse or overly noisy. Attempts to tune parameters like correlation window size, uniqueness ratio, and speckle settings have yielded inconsistent results. The user is seeking advice on missing pre-filtering steps or calibration issues specific to their camera setup.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Tuning StereoSGBM on PS5 Camera (ROS 2 Galactic) for Dense Depth Maps" reports on an attempt to tune StereoSGBM parameters within ROS 2 Galactic for dense depth map estimation from a PlayStation 5 stereo camera. The core finding involves difficulties in achieving smooth depth maps, as parameter adjustments resulted in outputs that were either overly sparse or excessively noisy. The methodology involved tuning settings such as the correlation window size, uniqueness ratio, and speckle settings in an effort to produce a point cloud suitable for 3D reconstruction using RTAB-Map. Attempts to refine the process indicated that missing pre-filtering steps or specific calibration issues related to the camera setup may be influencing the inconsistent results observed. This research suggests that specific hardware calibration and pre-processing are critical for reliable depth map generation from consumer camera systems.
